A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Syn4D research work. Their main texts, supplementary Sections 6–9, tables, figures, and equations are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on geometry-aware novel-view synthesis, reconstruction, tracking, depth estimation, and human pose estimation, including supplementary results in Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds matched-training-budget experiments in Table 9 and qualitative comparisons in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The dataset-generation pipeline, barycentric tracking representation, geometry-aware diffusion architecture, and downstream model adaptations remain unchanged. The additional experiments vary training-data budgets without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets and task coverage are retained. Table 9 reuses the Syn4D and ReCamMaster benchmarks; Figure 4 adds examples within the in-the-wild reconstruction and tracking coverage already present in v1.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds ReCamMaster itself as an evaluated comparator for visual quality and camera accuracy. v1's corresponding NVS tables compare only the authors' Kubric-trained and Syn4D-trained variants. The existing quantitative 4RC and MA-HMR comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 9.1 adds an experiment explicitly retraining the Kubric and Syn4D variants with matched budgets of 2,048 clips and the first 49 frames per clip, evaluated on both existing NVS benchmarks. Previously reported protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The new matched-budget control tests whether the NVS advantage persists after equalizing training-data quantities. Figure 4 adds comparative case studies of ball tracking and distant geometry with and without Syn4D training. Existing supplementary analyses, including GT-versus-DA3 conditioning, remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the model comparisons. Table 9 continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–8 are unchanged. New Table 9 reports matched-budget results: on ReCamMaster, FVD-V is 1,566 for Syn4D training versus 1,964 for Kubric; on Syn4D, FVD-V-P is worse at 566.5 versus 461.5. Figure 4 adds qualitative findings about tracking and distant geometry. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The DPM definitions, barycentric reconstruction equation, storage-complexity derivation, and supplementary correspondence-error definitions in Equations 2–3 are unchanged. No new assumptions, proofs, or mathematical results are introduced.

C1.justification: The central dataset, annotation, and downstream-benefit claims remain. However, the introduction drops the claimed licensing advantage and the assurance that all source data are licensed for AI training. It also changes the explicit claim to propose new tracking benchmarks and metrics into wording about supporting them.

C2.justification: Section 9.1 adds discussion of dataset-scale fairness and explains choosing ReCamMaster over SynCamMaster based on camera motion. Section 4.2 additionally attributes improved ball tracking and distant geometry to more complete and diverse annotations. The earlier interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes the explicit AI-training licensing assurance, leaving permitted reuse less clearly documented without establishing an actual license change. It also specifies the clip and frame selection for the new budget control. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time details in Section 7 are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to CAT3D, D2USt3R, VGGT-Omega, D4RT, and POMATO, and qualifies the description of earlier datasets as often containing only static scenes. These extend the research context without substantially changing Syn4D's positioning. Publication updates and duplicate references do not constitute additional distinct works.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and prose, consolidates three related-work subsections under Applications, replaces placeholder running headers, and adds acknowledgements. Most explanations and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 and Table 9, enlarges Figure 2's labels, and adjusts figure placement and table layout. The original supplementary Figures 4–10 are retained as Figures 5–11 with unchanged image content; their renumbering does not represent new evidence.

improvement.justification: The matched-budget control, explicit ReCamMaster comparison, and comparative visual examples modestly strengthen the empirical assessment while preserving earlier results. The benefit is limited: Table 9's broad winning claim needs qualification because Syn4D training loses one geometry metric and ReCamMaster has stronger visual scores. Removing the licensing assurance also leaves reuse terms less explicit, but the additional empirical scrutiny supports a modest net improvement.
